steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt together in a bowl. Set aside.

Beat 1 cup sugar and butter together in a large bowl with an electric mixer until light and fluffy; add flour mixture, alternating with milk, until no large lumps remain. Transfer batter to a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Arrange blackberries over batter; sprinkle with remaining 1 cup sugar. Pour boiling water over top.
Bake in the preheated oven until batter is set and berries are soft, about 50 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Emily's Blackberry Cobbler
raw_recipe.description: Emily's blackberry cobbler recipe is a simple blackberry cobbler featuring a fresh blackberry filling baked in a biscuit-like batter for a hot dessert.
raw_recipe.name: Emily's Blackberry Cobbler

review.reviewBody: I made this for my wife for Mothers Day. I was nervous about baking but it turned out great. She even liked it better than her berry cobbler that she has been making for years. We can't wait for fresh blackberries this summer! Awesome recipe!

This is a fascinating recipe. Instead of placing dollops of raw dough on top of the fruit, the raw dough goes on the bottom, and during baking rises to the top. I ran this procedure by a friend and she commented that this must be a very old recipe, indeed.

None-the-less, it turns out beautifully. I reduce the sugar to 2/3 cup in the final (third step), and it is sweet enough, especially with vanilla ice creme. Once cooled, it does form a purple gelatanous base, but this could be scraped off to lessen calories even further. 

We are swimming in blackberries and this recipe is one delicious, easy, and impressive way to use them. Any berry, fruit or rhubarb could be used.
So good!!! I used 3 cups of fruit (half blackberries, half blueberries) and like other reviewers suggested, I lessened the sugar on top to 3/4 cup. Turned out great!!!

It's very good. I didn't go exactly by the recipe. I melted the butter in the pan and poured a little in the batter because it was way to thick to pour. I added more milk to make it pourable. I mixed all the sugar in the batter using 1 cup sugar substitute and 1 cup regular sugar. I let it stay an additional 10 minutes for 1 hour cook time, trying to get it to brown more but that could have been the lack of real sugar. It's delicious.
Love it! Try substituting the butter with a 100 g pot of unsweetened apple puree. Works really well

Per the other reviews, I used a little less sugar and a little less water. It had a great flavor, and since the boiling water dissolved the sugar, which was on top, it had a very tiny sweet crunch. I'd love to find a cobbler with a crumbly topping on the top, but this will do for now. It is excellent with vanilla ice cream on top.
Definitely make again. I did add a tsp of cinnamon as suggested by others. Took to a potluck and it was the first dessert to go. Everyone loved it.
Way too much sugar for me, but otherwise liked it a lot. Will definitely make again, but with a quarter of the sugar in that last step.

First time making blackberry cobbler. I usually make peach. Blackberry is my new favorite! This was delicious topped with a scoop of vanilla ice-cream and some banana slices! The only changes were a little less sugar on top (I used about 3/4 cup) and I sprinkled a little blueberries on top with the blackberries.

I made this cobbler today for my husband and in-laws. I followed the recipe exactly. The breading part had a nice and tasty consistency but 2 cups of fresh blackberries did not make this dessert fruity enough for me. I served it warm with a dollop of vanilla ice cream, but there was too much cake to counter the fruit in my opinion. The recipe is quite simple and I will use it again, but next time I will at least double the fruit portion.

I made half of this recipe, using skim milk and slightly less sugar than it calls for because my wild berries were sweet. We loved the texture of the cake and how it looks when it's all nicely baked. Will make again!

I should have looked at the photos before I made this. I was looking for blackberry cobbler which is blackberries with a crust on top. What this is is it's a cake with a few blackberries sprinkled on top. And the cake was quite dry.
Very easy and very yummy!

I thought this was great. I just Sprinkled the top of the blackberries with sugar and only used 1 cup of boiling water. Oh I also added cinnamon to the flour mixture. Turned out delicious even without ice cream or whipped cream. We had it for breakfast!
good flavor but too much water. Next time I will only use half as much

This was the first time I have ever made a blackberry cobbler! Was a little nervous how it would turn out but it was delicious! I did add extra blackberries since this id my hubby’s favorite. Other than that I followed the recipe. Super delicious!
I love this recipe it came out soooo good. It’s our first time making cobbler so I was curious as the how it would come out. I was not disappointed, the recipe is easy to follow and taste great
Had high hopes, but it turned out pretty dry and maybe could have used a little more salt.
Huge hit with the family. Will definitely make again!
This recipe is just like what my Grandma useomake, I just changed pouring on top of boiling water to half of what they called for, it was amazing .. going to make again tonight
